generated_summary: HIV infection currently cannot be cured but can be controlled using combinations of multiple anti-retroviral drugs. These anti-retroviral drugs work together to manage the virus within the body. Because HIV genotypes vary between individual patients, it is difficult to determine which drug combination will be effective. Effective treatment must be tailored to the specific viral genotype of each person. Existing HIV drug resistance models typically rely only on sequence data and do not account for chemical similarity. Ignoring the chemical similarity of drugs means these models discard valuable information. Researchers applied proteochemometric models that combine chemical properties of drugs and protein target properties into one model. The mutation T216M was identified as a novel mutation that causes resistance to two drug classes.
